still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month and still printed on the branded box, though almost nobody pays it.

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent benefit, and Medicare still reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes.
The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands.
Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force.
The suicidal-ideation warning is still off the incretin labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: 43.0% ever-used minus 35.0% current = 8.0 points used and now off. About 15.0 points of current users (~43% of them) are on a second or later course, mostly 2032-era stoppers who came back on $29–49 generic semaglutide. 3.5 points cycled and are off again. (15.0 + 3.5) / 43.0 ≈ 43%. The remaining 4.5 points of off-drug adults stopped once and have not restarted. Ever-used rose 14.2 points, which is ~38.9M first-time users in two years. This fits one-year persistence of ~42% on generic weekly semaglutide (up from about one-third, because cost-driven stopping mostly ended; GI stopping did not) and ~50% restarting within a year. Age check: 0.20×22 + 0.33×36 + 0.24×46 + 0.23×33.5 = 4.4 + 11.9 + 11.0 + 7.7 ≈ 35.0. Income thirds average 35.0. Users: 35.0% of ~274M adults ≈ 95.9M. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~14.5M (15.1%, roughly flat in absolute terms; ~7.4M of them in monitored tracks), Medicare ~13.5M (14.1%, still code-gated), Medicaid ~3.6M (3.8%), legitimate cash ~55.3M (57.7%: ~36M on generic or authorised-generic semaglutide, ~15M on TrumpRx or direct branded products, ~4.3M on calm/focus plans), imported or counterfeit ~9.0M (9.4%). 14.5 + 13.5 + 3.6 + 55.3 + 9.0 = 95.9. The bottom third gained the most (+17 points) because legal generics replaced much of its gray use. Who is still off: about 14% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, down from ~23%. They are concentrated among uninsured adults without a telehealth or pharmacy routine, the rural Delta and Appalachia, and people who cannot fit $34–60 a month (pen plus visit fee) into budgets set by SNAP and rent. Adult obesity ~29.8%. Pediatric: ~1.9% of under-18s are on a drug, ~4.4% of 12–17s (mostly generic semaglutide on the adolescent label, much of it telehealth-prescribed). About 0.2% of 6–11s are on drug, and prepubertal starts kept falling. Around 0.3% of 12–17s use a parent's pen without a prescription, per poison-centre and claims-gap estimates, and these are not counted above. About 34M children under 18 live in a household with a current user, and ~5M live with a parent who has regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Structure unchanged. Medicare reaches ~13.5M users only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk (obesity plus CVD) codes, all behind prior authorisation, and now with generic-first step edits for semaglutide. FICTIONAL arithmetic: ~7.4M on generic semaglutide × ~$45 net = $333M/month, plus ~6.1M on branded products × ~$290 = $1,769M/month. Total ≈ $2.10B/month × 12 ≈ $25.2B a year in gross Part D incretin spend, down from ~$31.6B despite ~2.3M more users. The dementia route (tirzepatide, no generic) is ~2.3M × ~$250 × 12 ≈ $6.9B of that and is now the largest single line. Medicaid: the same 7 states cover weight-loss use, and ~3.6M Medicaid users are mostly on diabetes codes. The same two state programmes condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide sells for $3–25 a month across 120+ brands. Several of the same Hyderabad and Ahmedabad plants now hold US ANDAs. Chinese tirzepatide- and retatrutide-analogue vials sell for $15–50 where patents are not enforced. India and China supply about three-quarters of world incretin volume, and India now supplies most US generic semaglutide.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Generic semaglutide injection pens launched in the US in January 2033. FDA had approved ANDAs in December 2032 after the compound-patent exclusivity lapsed and Novo settled the device-patent litigation. Novo launched an authorised generic the same day. With 11 ANDA holders, cash prices fell from $59 at launch to $29–39 by mid-2034 at Walmart, Costco, Cost Plus and Kroger. A $15–25 telehealth visit is usually extra. Tirzepatide, retatrutide, MariTide, amycretin, survodutide, CagriSema and oral semaglutide remain branded. Novo cut the Wegovy pill to $99 starting and $129 maintenance on TrumpRx. Lilly cut Zepbound vials to $199 and Foundayo to $99–149. MariTide direct cash is $229. The $1,349 list price stands. Employer coverage stayed at 30%. Most non-covering employers simply point staff to $39 generics, and covering employers moved to generic-first formularies, so pharmacy trend fell without any change in who pays. Monitored metabolic tracks hold ~7.4M enrollees, all inside the ~14.5M commercial users, ~5.2M of them on clinic-administered MariTide or clinic-dosed generic. Total MariTide users ~5.4M. Route mix: weekly injectables ~62%, orals ~32%, monthly ~6%. The gray market did not shrink. It changed. Semaglutide vials largely disappeared from Telegram, and 'reta' and 'tirz' analogue vials at $40–60 plus counterfeit generic-semaglutide pens sold through pharmacy-styled sites now make up most of the ~9.0M users.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, plus US generics and authorised generic since Jan 2033)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: cardiovascular risk reduction (semaglutide incl. generics; tirzepatide)
adolescent obesity 12+ (semaglutide incl. generics, liraglutide, Wegovy pill); growth and pubertal-development precautions extended to adolescent labels Mar 2034
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, with growth-monitoring language)
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide); no extension
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm' and 'focus' microdosing through telehealth subscriptions, now mostly generic semaglutide micro-titrated pens plus low-dose orals, ~4.3M subscribers
alcohol reduction via telehealth and employer EAPs, continuing off-label after the Jun 2033 CRL
dementia-prevention use by 50–70-year-olds without CVD, now mostly on $39 generic semaglutide rather than cash tirzepatide
pre-emptive 'maintenance' use by adults with BMI 25–27 who were never obese
adolescent use of a parent's pen without a prescription (diversion, not prescribing)
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class or indication reached the US market in 2033–34. Oral semaglutide for AUD received a Complete Response Letter in Jun 2033. FDA cited loss of effect after discontinuation in the phase 3 extension and asked for reward-blunting data from the postmarketing study. Novo plans to resubmit in 2035. The bimagrumab-type lean-mass adjunct (filed Jul 2032) had its review extended after a major amendment on cardiac and dosing data, and its decision moved to Q1 2035, so it is not approved. Lilly's tirzepatide dementia confirmatory trial read out in Oct 2034, positive on the primary cognitive-decline endpoint with a fracture imbalance; no sNDA has been filed yet. Implant programmes are in phase 2 and not on the market. No oral matches tirzepatide. Generic semaglutide is a new source, not a new product class. Global incretin market ~$158B (2033): volume is up sharply, and value fell with US semaglutide genericisation.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now clearly the leading cause of stopping, since cost is no longer one for most users. Self-titrated generic users who jump doses report more severe early vomiting. Chronic diarrhoea in long-term users is routinely worked up for EPI.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained; generics carry identical labelling.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss. Absolute cholecystectomy volume rose with the user base.
Still no causal confirmation for acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Litigation centres on EPI and now names generic makers under the failure-to-update doctrine debates.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare cohort hip-fracture HR ~1.3 in users 65+ after more than 2 years, ~1.45 after three or more cycles. The fracture imbalance reappeared in the dementia confirmatory trial. Users 65+ on cash generics outside the Medicare codes get far fewer DXA scans.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained; DXA code in use; no adjunct approved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal in adults or adolescents. The adolescent psychiatric signal remains restrictive eating.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The FDA postmarketing observational study (Nov 2033, ~410,000 users) found clinically meaningful anhedonia at 7.6% vs 3.1% of matched controls at maintenance doses (adjusted HR ~2.1), with a dose-response, and ~10% on retatrutide. The low-dose stratum that resembles calm plans showed 4.4% vs 3.1%, with a confidence interval crossing null. Both platforms and critics cite it.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 'Anhedonia and emotional blunting' added to adverse reactions on all incretin labels (Jun 2034), not as a warning. FDA sent one warning letter to a calm platform over an explicit 'anxiety' claim (2034); untitled letters continue.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Fewer people now stop for cost, so regain now concentrates in GI stoppers, counterfeit-batch victims and people who lost a monitored-track place.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins the chronic-therapy framing and adherence monitoring.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users. It is more common among generic users with no clinician beyond a telehealth visit and no annual panel. Low ferritin in adolescent girls is confirmed in US claims.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language on labels, including generics.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after more than 5 years of continuous semaglutide (~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years). The exposed population is now far larger. A tirzepatide 6-year analysis (2034) shows ~1.3×, borderline significant.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide EPI warning carried to generics. Tirzepatide is under continued review, with no label change yet.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. Cycling effects on bone and pancreas remain poorly characterised, and the cheap-generic era multiplies short and repeated courses.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone, growth and pubertal postmarketing requirements continue, and generic ANDA holders now share in the pediatric registry funding.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: CDC MMWR (Oct 2033) attributed ~2,600 ED visits from Jan–Sep 2033 to counterfeit 'generic' semaglutide pens (wrong or no drug, non-sterile) and to Chinese retatrutide-analogue vials dosed in the wrong units, with 17 deaths. A legitimate ANDA holder recalled ~4.1M pens for particulate matter (Aug 2033); no injuries were confirmed. Adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~38,000. Poison-centre calls are ~8× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alert widened to analogue makers. FDA warning letter and recall at the ANDA plant. CBP seizures are up ~4× from 2030. Personal-importation enforcement is still weak, and no federal statute changed.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The liraglutide 6–11 PMR 36-month analysis (n≈3,100, Sep 2033) found the height-velocity deficit narrowing from ~0.7 to ~0.5 cm/year in year 3. Cumulative height is ~1.9 cm below expected, with bone age delayed ~0.6 years. That pattern is compatible either with later catch-up or with a lasting deficit, and final adult height is still unknown. The Nordic adolescent registry (Swedish and Danish, extended 2034) confirmed later pubertal onset in boys, found delayed menarche in girls started before 13 (median ~5 months), and kept the ARFID HR at ~1.8. US claims replicate the ARFID signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA extended growth and pubertal-development precautions (6-monthly height, Tanner staging, eating-disorder screening) to all adolescent semaglutide and liraglutide labels, including generics (Mar 2034). No age restriction. EMA added similar wording. The AAP reaffirmed lifestyle-first for prepubertal children. Utah and Louisiana require a documented in-person height measurement before a minor's incretin prescription.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: In the PMR DXA substudy and a Danish cohort, adolescents on semaglutide for 2+ years have lumbar BMD z-scores ~0.3 lower than BMI-matched peers. It is unclear how much reflects weight loss itself and how much is drug effect on peak bone mass accrual.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: New PMR for a DXA follow-up to age 25; no labelling beyond the general bone warning.

safety_ledger.effect: Accidental pediatric exposure and adolescent diversion of household product
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: With roughly half of households holding a pen, poison centres logged ~14,000 under-18 incretin exposures in 2033, about 3× 2031. Most were toddlers with a pen or pill, with hypoglycaemia rare but vomiting common. A growing minority were 13–17-year-olds self-injecting a parent's generic pen.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA requested child-resistant packaging for oral products; pen carton warnings updated; no restriction.

food_and_beverage.state: About half of US households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~16% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~14%. Dollar sales are down ~3% in real terms as premium mix no longer offsets volume. The zip-code split stopped working: once $39 generics reached lower-income areas, Kroger's and Albertsons' value-pack bays in those stores lost volume faster than the protein bays in the suburbs, and both chains are re-planning a second time. General Mills and Kraft Heinz cut plant shifts. Protein is mainstream and cheapening, and pea protein capacity has caught up.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~19% from 2025 and beer ~12%. Heavy-drinker losses spread down the income ladder with generic access, while alcohol reduction stays an off-label telehealth product after the AUD CRL. Bar closures have spread from Midwestern mid-sized cities to Southern ones. Non-alcoholic 'calm' drinks grow but are under 3% of the category.

restaurants.state: Traffic is down ~3–4% from 2032. QSR value menus, which had grown in lower-income markets on gray-market regainers, softened as legal generics held those customers on drug. Portion-tiered menus are the industry norm. Breakfast and coffee dayparts hold up best.

apparel.state: Size runs are being re-set downward a second time, now in lower-income zips. Plus-size specialists consolidate. Resale and stretch serve cyclers. Premium structured athletic wear and tailoring for 'built' bodies carry the margins.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. Budget chains (Planet Fitness, Crunch) gained the most, selling $29–39 'lean-mass' add-ons to new generic users. Premium DXA-plus-coaching runs $250–400 a month. Employer tracks bundle InBody scans with clinic dosing.

insurance.state: Employer weight-loss coverage is flat at 30%. Generic-first formularies cut pharmacy trend to ~+2%. Employers that had dropped coverage did not return, because pointing staff to $39 cash is cheaper than administering a benefit. Adherence and BMI-progress differentials spread to state employee plans in Georgia and Tennessee and to more self-insured mid-sized firms. Part D incretin spend fell (~$25B) and Part D premiums held flat for 2034. Pediatric prior authorisation requires growth charts, which cash buyers bypass.

pharma.state: Novo's US semaglutide revenue fell ~40% after generics. It survives on the authorised generic, the Wegovy pill and CagriSema. Lilly grows on tirzepatide's dementia route and retatrutide. Amgen grows on employer tracks. Indian ANDA holders (11 of them) ship most US generic volume on thin margins. Counterfeit defence and serialisation spending tops $1B industry-wide.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness alone no longer signals anything, because it costs $39. What signals is everything around it. Muscle, DXA reports and a branded molecule (retatrutide, MariTide via the employer clinic) mean money or a good job. Thin and soft with no muscle is 'generic thin', the default body of the median worker. A sallow look with a shaky regain history means Telegram vials. Being heavy after 50 now reads less as lost access than as refusal, or as being unreachable by any pharmacy routine. Among upper-tier parents, an unmedicated child with a normal growth curve is the status document.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: In Charlotte and Austin, lean-mass percentage and 'off-drug lean' remain the elite boasts, and people say 'generic thin' with a small sneer. Along the Columbus logistics corridor the plant clinic now doses generic semaglutide for new hires and MariTide for leads, and shift workers can tell which is which. In Memphis, which had the fastest gray-market growth in 2031–32, the body changed in a year as $34 Kroger pens replaced Telegram vials, and the cycler's face is giving way to the generic body. The people left visibly heavy in Shelby County are mostly older, uninsured or without a phone-based pharmacy routine. Bethesda and Plano parents keep prepubertal children off drug, while teenagers in Shelby County and the Columbus suburbs start on telehealth generics with height measured, if at all, against a door frame.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter everywhere, not only in the suburbs. Church potlucks in Memphis shrank to dessert-free 'fellowship plates'. Bread Alone claims ~800 congregations and runs youth retreats framed around the growth data. School-lunch fights moved to whether schools should flag students who eat almost nothing at lunch.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'On generic' is a neutral dating-app field. 'Off-drug lean' and 'lean-mass verified' are premium badges. Calm-plan tags are common and divisive: some users filter them out, and others filter for them. The weekly pen day and the monthly clinic day organise couples' calendars.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is treated as a utility to be managed for $39, and craving as a minor equipment failure. Visible hunger in an adult reads as either poverty or principle. The counter-movement split further. Unmuted runs on class and calm-plan critique, the MAHA wing runs on children's bones and puberty, and fat-acceptance revivalists hold onto a shrinking constituency, mostly older and rural.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The FDA postmarketing study (Nov 2033) found anhedonia at 7.6% vs 3.1% of controls at maintenance doses, ~10% on retatrutide, and 4.4% vs 3.1% (not significant) in the low-dose stratum. Applied to ~91M maintenance-dose users, the excess implies roughly 4M Americans with clinically meaningful drug-attributable anhedonia, most of whom never present. About 4.3M people pay for calm/focus plans. Level's 'Quiet Weekly' and its copycats sell micro-titrated generic semaglutide pens at $29–39 plus a $19–39 platform fee, and low-dose orals at $99–129 plus a fee.
interior_life.framing: Platforms: 'quiet you can afford', 'focus for the price of a streaming service'. Manufacturers and generic makers say nothing and let the label speak. HR says 'steadiness'. Clinicians now point to the adverse-reaction line on the label. Unmuted calls it 'the $39 sedative'. Platforms quote the null low-dose stratum as safety evidence.
interior_life.effect_on_work: ~7.4M employees in adherence-verified tracks. Georgia and Tennessee state employees joined in 2033–34. An Ohio federal court dismissed the lead ADA case in Apr 2034, holding the tracks voluntary under the wellness safe harbour. Call-centre and logistics promotions informally favour enrollees. In knowledge firms 'focus protocol' is listed beside sleep scores, and two benefit brokers sell employers access to calm-platform focus-cohort analytics, de-identified and opt-in.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off' memoir outsells 'flat' fiction. A small genre of 'generic diaries' from first-time working-class users finds readers. Unmuted off nights run in Detroit, Baltimore, Memphis and now Columbus. Sportsbook handle per active account fell again, now in lower-income markets too. Streaming services commission 'ambient' slates aimed at calm-plan households.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Desire mismatch is still the leading couples-therapy complaint. The cheap pen makes 'matching' common: partners start a calm plan to close the gap with a medicated spouse. Some therapists now ask about dose before asking about the marriage.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Adherence conditioning is now framed as fairness: at $39 a month, legislators in Atlanta and Nashville argue, non-adherence is a choice. Illinois remains the only state ban. MAHA-aligned legislators passed in-person height-measurement laws in Utah and Louisiana, the first state action on minors. Calm marketing produces hearings and one FDA warning letter. Medicated and unmedicated voters are now sorted more by age and rurality than by income.

state.regulatory_posture: Routine and permissive, with more enforcement. FDA approved generic semaglutide, issued a CRL on oral semaglutide for AUD, extended the bimagrumab-type review, added anhedonia to adverse reactions, extended pediatric growth precautions to adolescent labels, and issued one calm-plan warning letter. Utah and Louisiana require in-person height measurement for minors' prescriptions. Congress created no coverage, mandate or importation rule.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No new subsidy or coverage. TrumpRx still operates on manufacturer-set prices. The 2027 tri-agency 30% guidance stands and has been adopted by state employee plans in Georgia (~700k covered lives) and Tennessee (~300k). Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Deeper in practice and now upheld in court. Clinic dosing records, PBM fills, generic-pharmacy loyalty data and telehealth mood check-ins flow to wellness vendors under consent. The April 2034 Ohio ruling treats the tracks as voluntary wellness programmes. Calm platforms sell de-identified focus cohorts to benefit brokers.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE rules unchanged. The Army recruit oral pilot continues. DOT still has not ruled on off-label alcohol-reduction or calm-plan use among commercial drivers, and some carriers now test for it in post-accident panels without any rule requiring it.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India now supplies most legal US generic semaglutide from FDA-inspected plants, and the same industrial base supplies the gray market. The Aug 2033 particulate recall at a Hyderabad ANDA plant drew congressional letters about dependence. China's analogue makers moved to retatrutide copies, and the FDA import alert named more of them. US–India talks still list mail enforcement without agreement. The US gap between cash generic and Indian generic is ~3–10×, down from 40–50×; the gap for branded tirzepatide or retatrutide versus analogue vials is ~5–25×.

events.event: Generic semaglutide pens reach US pharmacies at $59 a month, a month after FDA approved the first ANDAs once exclusivity lapsed and Novo settled the device-patent suits; Novo launches an authorised generic, and with 11 makers in the market the cash price falls to $29–39 by mid-2034
FDA rejects oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder, citing loss of effect after stopping and missing reward-blunting data, and extends its review of the first muscle-preserving adjunct into 2035

CDC links about 2,600 emergency visits and 17 deaths in nine months to counterfeit 'generic' semaglutide pens and mis-dosed Chinese retatrutide copies, weeks after a legitimate Indian generic maker recalls 4.1 million pens for particles

FDA's postmarketing study finds anhedonia more than twice as common at maintenance doses but no significant excess at low doses; calm-plan platforms cite the low-dose result in ads, and Level's $34 'Quiet Weekly' generic pen pushes calm subscriptions past 4 million

Three-year growth data show children started on liraglutide before puberty are ~1.9 cm shorter than expected with delayed bone age, and Nordic registries tie early semaglutide to later menarche; FDA extends growth and puberty monitoring to all adolescent labels including generics as teen use nears 4.4%

An Ohio federal court dismisses the lead ADA challenge to an employer's adherence-verified metabolic track, months after Georgia and Tennessee began charging state employees up to 30% more if they lack verified adherence or BMI progress

open_tensions: Teen use has nearly doubled on $39 generics, often prescribed by telehealth with no one measuring. The 3-year data are compatible with either catch-up growth or permanently shorter adults, and only Utah and Louisiana require anyone to check.

Cheap legal semaglutide pushed the gray market up the potency ladder rather than out. About 9 million people use retatrutide and tirzepatide copies or counterfeit 'generic' pens, and the plants making legal US generics share a supply base with the ones making fakes.

With the drug costing $39, adherence conditioning has a new fairness argument and a court win. State employee plans in Georgia and Tennessee may be the template for other states, and Illinois still stands alone.

Over 4 million people pay for low-dose calm. The only federal data say the low-dose harm is too small to detect, the maintenance-dose harm is real, and the line between them is a titration schedule that users can move themselves.

prose.headline: The $39 Body: One in Three Americans Is on the Shot Now. Nobody Is Sure Who's Measuring the Children
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 roughly one American adult in three takes an incretin drug, close to ninety-six million people. Almost half of all adults have tried one. The number nearly doubled in two years for one reason: in January 2033 semaglutide became generic. Eleven manufacturers, most of them in India, now sell the weekly pen, and Novo sells its own authorised generic beside them. By the middle of this year the price at Walmart, Costco and Kroger had settled between twenty-nine and thirty-nine dollars a month. The branded box still says $1,349, and almost nobody pays it.

Nothing about who pays changed. Medicare still covers the drugs only for diabetes, heart, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk patients, and its incretin spending fell to about twenty-five billion dollars as generics replaced brands. Employers still cover weight loss at three firms in ten. Most of the rest simply tell staff where the cheap pen is. More than half of all users now pay cash for themselves, and for most of the country the question is no longer whether you can afford the drug. It is whether thirty-four dollars and a telehealth visit fit into the month, and for the people who are still heavy, mostly older, rural or uninsured, they often do not.

The gray market did not die. It moved up. Telegram shops that once sold semaglutide vials now sell copies of the triple agonist retatrutide for forty dollars, often labelled in the wrong units, alongside counterfeit generic pens on websites dressed as pharmacies. Last year the CDC tied about 2,600 emergency visits and seventeen deaths to those products. A legitimate Indian generic maker recalled four million pens for particles in the same months. Nobody was hurt by the recall, but it was noticed in Congress, where nothing followed.

Calm is cheaper too. Level's thirty-four-dollar Quiet Weekly pen, a micro-titrated generic, helped push calm and focus subscriptions past four million. The FDA's own study found anhedonia more than twice as common at full doses and no significant excess at low ones, and the platforms now quote the second half of that sentence in their ads. Anhedonia is listed on the labels as an adverse reaction, and the agency sent one warning letter.

The children's numbers grew more complicated. Three years in, children who started liraglutide before puberty are about two centimetres shorter than expected, but their bones are also younger, which could mean they will catch up or could mean nothing at all. Nordic registries tie early semaglutide to later puberty. The FDA now tells doctors to measure every teenager on the drug every six months. Teen use has nearly doubled anyway, mostly on generic pens prescribed by telehealth. Utah and Louisiana require someone to measure the child in person first, and no other state does.

Bodies have stopped meaning thin and started meaning everything around thin. In Charlotte and Austin people say 'generic thin' the way they once said 'off the rack', and the boast is muscle on a scan. Along the Columbus freight corridor the plant clinic doses generic pens for new hires and MariTide for shift leads. In Memphis, the gray-market capital of 2031, faces changed within a year as Kroger replaced Telegram. The people left visibly heavy there are mostly people no pharmacy routine reaches.

At thirty-nine dollars, adherence has become a moral argument. Georgia and Tennessee now charge state workers up to thirty percent more without verified adherence or progress, and an Ohio court said that is voluntary. From a distance the country looks lighter and quieter than it has in fifty years, and few people are asking what that cost.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tasha Greer wakes at five-ten in Frayser, North Memphis, and does her pen before coffee, left thigh, Thursday. The pen is from Kroger, thirty-four dollars, a name on the label she can't pronounce. Last year it was a vial from a man on Telegram, and one month the vial was cloudy. She doesn't think about that month anymore.

She drives to Mrs. Odom's in Raleigh, bathes her, makes her grits. Mrs. Odom is eighty-one and eats all of them. Tasha watches her eat with a feeling she can't name.

At lunch she sits in the car with a protein shake and a phone call from her sister Dee, who is on something called reta now, forty dollars, because the generic 'stopped doing anything.' Dee sounds fine. Dee always sounds fine.

The agency texts: new client in Bartlett, starts Monday. The agency doesn't cover anything. Nobody she knows has a job that does, except her cousin at the FedEx hub, who gets his shot from a nurse and has to swipe a badge to prove it.

At four she picks up Marcus, thirteen, from practice. He has been on the generic since his twelfth birthday, a telehealth doctor, nineteen dollars a visit, nobody ever weighed him in person. He's quiet in the car. He's always quiet now, and she can't tell if that's thirteen.

After dinner, half a plate each, she stands him against the kitchen door frame and makes a pencil mark over his head. It is a quarter inch above the March mark. She looks at it a long time, then writes the date.
